old_title: Man United latest: Pochettino speaks after agreeing deal to succeed Carrick
new_title: Man United latest: Tearful Pochettino explains why he ditched USA to replace Carrick

Mauricio Pochettino has agreed to become the new Manchester United manager and will face the media for the first time since Michael Carrick's sacking as he concludes his time as United States boss.
A second Old Trafford comeback of the week, this time battling from two goals down twice to rescue a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on Sunday, was not enough to save Carrick's job and the club announced on Thursday that it had parted ways with him after just 10 games of the season and with his side 18th during the international break.
The Independent reported that contact was made with Pochettino over succeeding Carrick on Monday and the Argentinian is now on the verge of returning to the Premier League after reaching a reported agreement with the club.
But with USMNT having two Nations League matches with Haiti in the docket this international break, Pochettino could still be set to lead his team for these upcoming fixtures before reporting to Carrington shortly afterwards, something he may address at today's press conference.
Follow all the latest updates in our live blog below:
Mauricio Pochettino conference coming up
We're expecting Mauricio Pochettino to arrive for his press conference in the next few minutes.
The USMNT manager will no doubt face questions on the Manchester United role he is on the verge of taking.
The ultimate Michael Carrick mistake that left his Man United dream doomed
When Manchester United finally decided to push ahead with plans to appoint Mauricio Pochettino after a decade of interest, two considerations were key. One was "experience" of a club of this size. Another was "something extra".
That latter idea had previously formed one of the concerns that some of the United hierarchy had about Carrick on appointing him for the full-time job back in spring. The thinking at the time was that the former midfielder would offer the stability that everyone was talking about, surely returning United to the Champions League that season, but they wondered whether he had the "x factor" for a proper title push. Many felt there was opportunity, because of how many big clubs were going through periods of upheaval, with Pep Guardiola's exit at Man City, while Xabi Alonso and Andoni Iraola begun adventures at Chelsea and Liverpool respectively.
They just didn't expect United to be one of them. The speed of the collapse has shocked the club leadership.
Five key problems Mauricio Pochettino must solve first at Manchester United
Mauricio Pochettino is becoming the latest manager of Manchester United following the sacking of Michael Carrick.
Carrick's permanent tenure lasted just three months, and he departs the club with United 18th in the Premier League, having won just once in the top flight since the start of the season.
Pochettino will inherit a bruised and battered squad lacking in confidence and in dire need of inspiration in order to turn around their fortunes.
Pochettino's first match is a trip to Liverpool, and the performance at Anfield could be the catalyst for an uptick in United's fortunes.
There are plenty of problems facing Pochettino when he arrives at Old Trafford, both on and off the pitch, but he must tackle these five in the short term to rebuild confidence in his squad...
Harry Redknapp backs Mauricio Pochettino to revive 'real mess' Man Utd
Former Spurs manager Harry Redknapp told Sky Sports: "Someone said to me today, 'What a bad time to take the job', I said, 'I could never think of a better time to take over the Man United job'.
"They are rock-bottom. There's only one way, it's up.
"It isn't like David Moyes following Alex Ferguson. David Moyes is a great manager, but following Fergie was impossible.
"Now he (Pochettino) takes over a club that is in a real mess at the moment, and he can only take one take them one way, and that is going to be up.
"I like him. He's a great character, very clever manager, knows the game, and I'm sure he'll do a good job.
"But it's going to be two or three years before you see Man United anywhere near what you'd hope they would be."
Mauricio Pochettino's credentials
Mauricio Pochettino began his managerial career at Espanyol before moving to Southampton for a 16-month spell in charge.
The Argentine was then appointed as manager of Tottenham in the summer of 2014 and established them as a top four club, taking them to the Champions League final in 2019 before being dismissed less than six months afterwards.
He won three trophies as manager of Paris Saint-Germain including the 2021/22 Ligue 1 title.
In 2023/24 he spent a season as Chelsea boss before being fired in the summer.
Pochettino then replaced Gregg Berhalter as United States Men's National Team head coach in 2024, following the side's group-stage exit from the Copa America. He has won 21 of his 35 matches in charge and took the nation to the last-16 of the World Cup this summer.
Sir Alex Ferguson's endorsement of Mauricio Pochettino
Sir Alex Ferguson is already a known fan of Mauricio Pochettino.
"Well the manager has been fantastic," the Scot said back in 2016, with Pochettino then linked with the job several times since 2018.
"They have a bad record of managers, there is no doubt about that. They have had so many over the years, but this lad has composure.
"You never see him ruffled and the way his team play is a testimony to the work he is doing.
"The most important thing for English football is how many English and young players are in his team.
"He understands the advantage of playing young people. They won't let you down and they have been fantastic."
How Michael Carrick's fate was sealed
Michael Carrick has been at serious peril of the sack for nearly three weeks now.
Back-to-back humiliations against Como and Bournemouth, two defeats by three goals, left the Manchester United hierarchy discussing next steps in crisis talks at Carrington on Monday 26 October.
Carrick, who was at the United training ground that day watching the U21s, survived those talks and was kept on the manage the trip to Chelsea, which ended in a 2-0 defeat despite signs of improvement.
He clung on by the skin of his teeth in the 3-2 comeback win against Roma in midweek, which could have easily been Carrick's final game in charge if not for Matheus Cunha's late heroics.
And while United left it late again on the weekend, scoring two goals in stoppage time to salvage a 4-4 draw against Villa, the resumption of crisis talks in Monaco this week spelled the end for Carrick, with Jim Ratcliffe and the United upper brass calling time on his reign.
Gary Neville explains why Mauricio Pochettino is the right manager for Man United
Gary Neville has spoken on the news that Mauricio Pochettino will become the new manager of Manchester United following the sacking of Michael Carrick on Thursday.
"I've always, and I think this is public knowledge... I've always wanted Mauricio Pochettino as manager at [Manchester] United," said Neville.
"I've said that numerous times, back when Jose Mourinho was maybe coming to Manchester United, I think maybe when Erik ten Hag came to Manchester United.
"I think he's a brilliant person, I think he'll handle the media, I think he understands the size of the club but it's a monumental task to win everybody else over and get everybody on side and make sure he has a team that can compete.
"But he's a brilliant coach with great experience and he's a good man. And I think he also believes in young players and bringing players through and developing them and coaching them, which is what he's going to have to do at Manchester United.
"I've always liked Mauricio Pochettino, whether this is the right point for him to take the Manchester United job, who knows?
"We'll find out in the next year or two but I'm hoping that he's made some pretty strong demands on the way in and he's got control of the club."
USA make Pep Guardiola 'top target' to replace Mauricio Pochettino
Now this is ambitious.
Pep Guardiola is a "top target" to become the next USA head coach with Mauricio Pochettino leaving the role to become Manchester United manager.
Man Utd's worst start
Manchester United have made their worst start to a season in 40 years under Michael Carrick this year.
They've won just once in the Premier League, against Ipswich Town, and have gained only eight points from the first 10 matches.
Pressure has mounted increasingly on Carrick over recent weeks though United are unbeaten in their last two games with a 3-2 win over Roma in the Champions League followed by a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa on Sunday.
That win over Roma is United's only victory, across all competitions, in their last 11 games.

Mauricio Pochettino has agreed to become the new Manchester United manager after Michael Carrick's sacking.
A second Old Trafford comeback of the week, this time battling from two goals down twice to rescue a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on Sunday, was not enough to save Carrick's job and the club announced on Thursday that it had parted ways with him after just 10 games of the season and with his side 18th during the international break.
Former Chelsea and Tottenham boss Pochettino has now been confirmed as Carrick's replacement, bringing his reign as USA manager to a close at the end of the international break.
He was tearful about leaving the USA in a press conference on Friday but said an opportunity the size of United is "difficult to turn down".
Follow all the latest updates in our live blog below:
Recap: Man Utd confirm Mauricio Pochettino start date after deal agreed to succeed Michael Carrick
The club confirmed their decision to sack Michael Carrick after just 10 games of the season on Thursday, with the club dwindling in 18th heading into the international break.
United have paid US Soccer compensation worth an initial $7m (£5.3m) to get Pochettino out of his existing contract, which ran until the 2030 World Cup. Additional compensation will be required for Pochettino's trusted coaching staff, including long-time assistant Jesus Perez.
Mauricio Pochettino reveals when he was contacted about replacing Michael Carrick
Mauricio Pochettino said he received contact from Manchester United on Sunday about possibly taking over as manager.
Michael Carrick was not officially sacked until Thursday.
"All was so quick," he said. "Sunday afternoon, there started to be some contact. We were very transparent [with US Soccer].
"We'll have time next week to talk about the job at Manchester United. It's much better to talk now about US Soccer."
Tearful Mauricio Pochettino explains why he swapped USA for Man Utd
How Mauricio Pochettino's Man United could line up against Liverpool
Mauricio Pochettino is the new head coach of Manchester United having agreed to take over following the sacking of Michael Carrick.
His first game in charge will be at the cauldron of Anfield to take on Liverpool on Sunday 22 November and, not only is it a contest imbued with history and rivalry, but it is also a match that United must show signs of improvement in.
Here's how his first team could shape up:
Pochettino leaves
That's all from Mauricio.
His parting message to the press pack: "Thank you guys. Honour to be with you."
Pochettino wanted to take charge of Haiti games out of respect for his team
"Before being a professionals we are people," he said. "The emotional link between us that we built in these two years is to show the commitment and respect and, and the care and the love even if we took a decision that, for one party, is maybe not the best.
"We were open, you know, because I think we have the respect of the players and the staff, and they understand the situation.
"If Manchester United and the Federation agreed on different terms, I would need to respect the agreement, but this has happened and of course all the games are important."
Pochettino asked why he signed contract extension with USA
"It's obvious," he replied. "I never say that I want to fall back.
"They know there's not too many opportunities that can happen in your career the size of Manchester United, and when that happens, it's difficult to turn down that situation."
US Soccer chief says windfall from release clause will be put towards new coach
US Soccer CEO JT Batson said: "The agreement with Manchester United, those funds US Soccer is a non-profit. Those funds are used to hire great coaches, invest in youth development."
Pochettino staying tight-lipped about Man Utd move
"I will have time next week to talk about the job at Manchester United," he said. "But now it's much better to talk about us, USA Soccer.
"We now have two games ahead and now is complete focus on this."
Pochettino: 'We were very transparent'
"We were very transparent," he said.
"We were talking with the federation. Yesterday when things were positive in the way that the agreement was, we had a meeting and I communicated to the player and the whole staff.
"The decision is between the federation and Manchester United that we continue with our job in the camp.
"I think we will have time next week to talk about the job at Manchester United. Now I think it is better to talk about USA soccer and the national team. We have two games ahead and the focus is completely on this."
